Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is universally open
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable}), and
\item for every morphism of algebraic spaces $Z \to Y$ the morphism of
topological spaces $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$f$ is universally open
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable}), and

for every morphism of algebraic spaces $Z \to Y$ the morphism of
topological spaces $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open.

reason: The universal-open condition for representable f can be checked after an étale scheme chart of Y. The comparison square for any algebraic-space Z has open surjective horizontal arrows and a surjective map to the topological fibre product, allowing openness to descend to |Z×_YX|→|Z|.

Use the chapter’s definition of algebraic-space morphisms on the chosen big fppf site; a representable morphism has a property P only through all its scheme-base-change tests.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is universally open,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open, and
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a universally open morphism
of algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is universally open.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$.
conclusions:
for every scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open,

for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is open, and

there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is a universally open morphism
of algebraic spaces, and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is universally open.

reason: The source explicitly omits proofs of (1)⇒(2) and (2)⇒(3) at line 802. It develops substantial arguments for (3)⇒(4), (4)⇒(1), and Zariski locality, but the two omitted implications are part of the asserted equivalence.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $p : X \to \Spec(k)$ be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$ where $k$ is a field. Then
$p : X \to \Spec(k)$ is universally open.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $p : X \to \Spec(k)$ be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$ where $k$ is a field.

reason: An étale scheme presentation U→X gives a universally open map U→Spec k by the scheme theorem. Base change of this surjective étale cover remains surjective, and a composite open map with surjective first factor forces the induced map X×_kZ→Z to be open for every scheme Z.
